reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
The number of employees is “full party,” there is a lot of kindness, and the traffic is a bit rush hour.
The chef who explained it had an ASMR tone, so I needed subtitles for half of it.
There was an incident where I brought expensive wine and the glass was switched while drinking. Strangely enough, my first thought was, “Will I come again?”

Dinner 240,000 won, corkage 33,000 won.
It's not an easy price, but Shari's food confirmed once again that my taste buds are attached to Korean-style sushi.
Whether it's clams or not, the soup filled with clams is the type that refreshes your stomach.

The appetizer starts with the ‘Country Road Hangover Edition’.
Chawanmushi with soup warms your body as warm eggs slide down your throat.

Among the three types of sashimi, the red sea bream is struck with both hands for a savory and soft flavor, and the black sea bream is savored with the scent of the sea breeze, covering the tongue with umami.
The belly of black sea bream takes the taste to the next level by adding a chewy texture.
Snow crab meat is made by mixing the legs and body and is sufficiently savory even without sauce, but because Korea makes crab meat so well, there comes a strange moment when the ‘scarcity of snow crab’ becomes rare.

The stewed octopus is sweeter than expected, but the chewy but not tough texture is GOAT.
The grilled clams have zero fishiness and are delightfully chewy, salty, and savory, as if “a hundred lilies were concentrated in one bite.”
The firey scent of the grilled anago did a good job of suppressing the fishiness, and the happiness of the Geumtae rice bowl that followed started from the moment the thick Geumtae oil coated the rice grains.

Nigiri is a standard flow.
The red sea bream awakens the tongue, and the flounder had bad luck today (it came out after the red sea bream and suffered a loss).
Kelp-pickled sweet shrimp are ‘just delicious sweet shrimp’—the sweetness has been brought out well by aging.

Akami has a good balance of 0 fish and not too much saltiness, and the raw scallops are sliced ​​thick like fish, clearly showing off the charm of ‘rough scallops.’
Herring is a textbook adjustment that turns the fishy taste into flavor.
Uni seaweed roll is today’s ‘seaweed’s victory’—on days when Uni is weak, seaweed becomes the main character.

On the contrary, the tuna belly meat is the best this year.
It sticks well to Shari without any stress or fishiness.
Personally, the salmon roe seaweed roll had a weak presence, but the piece of minced tuna wrapped in seaweed was fun, like “the essence of high-quality tuna kimbap.”

Eel sushi is different from anago and gives a satisfying feeling of ‘freshwater stub + oil’.
The Bakgoji seaweed roll today was thin and had a faint character, and the Gyoku had a very nice castella texture with a slight glaze on the top.
The last gizzard shad is a style that deliberately emphasizes the fishy texture, so there are definitely likes and dislikes - I like it, so I think I put it at the very end of the course.

reviews.text:
#Sinsa-dong #hormones

“Considering the price, it’s a 100-point perfect drink snack.”

The second season of Black and White Chef is streaming now.
The top 7 are already about to be decided, but 93 participants have already been eliminated from the battlefield.
There are a lot of people caught on the screen, but there are also quite a few whose names are only glimpsed.
Sinsa-dong's Horumon is also a Black and White Chef contestant and only has one line of his name on the screen, but this restaurant opened in Cheongdam-dong almost 7 years ago and has remained popular to this day.

I chose this restaurant for a year-end gathering with friends, and one of the reasons is that I am concerned that it will become difficult to visit this place once the black and white chef starts, but I am more curious about the 45,000 won course meal.

#Course
The composition of the 45,000 won course is as follows.

Two cold appetizers
- Smots: Pickled intestines - Good sour taste and texture. It's great as a starting mouthwash.
- Shiro Senmai: The leaves are trimmed and seasoned until they are white and fragrant. As expected, the texture is great and the sesame oil smells good.

two roasted things
- Hatsuyaki: Pan-fry the heart of the heart into diced pieces. It's a shame it's a little hard.
- Motsuyaki: Grilled beef intestines on only one side to bring out the chewiness, savory flavor, and softness of the fat.

Two nabe dishes
- Sukiyaki: Eat beef sukiyaki with the aorta and another internal organ added. The sukiyaki is not authentic and feels like a sweet nabe, but it is not bad because the two internal organs add to the texture.

main meat

reviews.text:
#Sinsa-dong #Goryoriken

“Kim Gun’s style confirmed”

I made an early reservation and visited Goryoriken for my wife's birthday.
It's been a while since I made the reservation, but as a big fan, I was very happy to see that Chef Geon Kim was included in the cast, and after that, reservations at Goryori Ken became extremely difficult. It was truly a lucky reservation and visit.

I became a big fan of Ichie's amazing skill in handling ingredients and creative menus from the time he opened, and since then I have been following him to Goryori Ken, Hoehyeon Restaurant, and Hoehyeon Cafe to taste the taste of Kim Geon.

When you first opened Goryori Ken, you experienced the birth of a wonderful Japanese restaurant that embodies your passion for cooking.
When I visited Goryoriken for the second time, I recruited Louis Sainteque's sauce master and added sauce to Japanese food to complete a French-style course. It was awkward, but delicious.
On this third visit, the awkwardness of the second time was completely gone and I was introduced to a Michelin 1-star restaurant that creates amazing seafood dishes.

#Hospitality
Compared to my last visit, customer service has changed noticeably.
First of all, there was no menu, but there was a board introducing the seafood ingredients of the day.
And when the food is served, Chef Geon Kim personally explains the food.
It's visually nice to be able to see the food being prepared in the open kitchen.
Another difference is that Chef Gun Kim personally serves the food and refills the drinks.
How many restaurants are there where the head chef personally serves the food and fills the drinks?
It can be said that this house has a solid Goryoriken style and a feeling of being treated well.

#Cooking Philosophy
It seems like you have a firm direction for cooking.
For basic seafood ingredients, seasonal ingredients in Korea are used as much as possible.
It consists only of seafood, no poultry or meat.

We complete the dish using the optimal recipe and sauce that makes each ingredient delicious. During this process, we continuously research recipes and sauces to create new dishes.
If the food from my last visit was French-Japanese cuisine that combines sauces with Japanese food, the food from this visit feels like a complete dish.

#mackerel
A French-style dish where you eat well-seasoned saba with lily root milk sauce.
A wonderful dish with added flavor and aroma with Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese and arugula.
Shimesaba has a slight mackerel flavor, but depending on your taste, it may be perceived as flavor or fishiness.

#Cream #Monkfish
It was a shame that the prawns were a bit dry, but I liked the richness of the large seasonal prawns and the ankimo marinated in sake and milk, and the sweetness and freshness of the champagne jelly balanced it out. The symbolism of the season is highlighted with sweet persimmons and shine muskets.

#overthrow
An Italian-style dish made with steamed abalone marinated in oil.
The fragrant aroma of a large amount of herbs, the flavor of olive oil, and the soft abalone combine well.
The curry-like barley adds an accent to the carbohydrates.
Abalone can also be used excellently as an Italian ingredient.

#freshwater eel
Freshwater eel grilled on binchotan charcoal was full of flavor without any fishy taste.
The gently grilled kabayaki is made softer with red potato puree, and cauliflower-oil stew adds texture.
If you eat it with onions and burdock stewed in soy sauce, it's a wonderful fusion of Japanese and Western food.

#tilefish #blue crab
20 crabs are boiled down a day to create a thick crab sauce.
The bread with scales on top of crab crystals made with only the flavor of blue crab without adding salt is topped with a large piece of deep-fried tilefish, and the plainness of the world is as new as if you were dressed in the ocean.
Paprika adds texture, and seasonal whole burdocks delight the palate.
A godsend is pasta with a few lines.
The magic of turning a simple dish into the world’s most delicious crab pasta.

#cutlassfish
Thick cutlassfish grilled on binchotan charcoal is combined with a slightly spicy dashi that has been brewed wonderfully and a sauce thickened with arrowroot starch.
The cool and spicy sauce gives the perfect hangover effect, and the lean cutlassfish meat is cozy.
Seasonal colors are beautifully decorated with fried seaweed.

#Samfish
Mackerel caught with a fish is grilled with butter in French style, and grilled maitake mushrooms on the side add texture.
The garnish made with stir-fried shiitake mushrooms has a truffle-like scent that stimulates the sense of smell, and the slightly spicy sauce made with button mushrooms and shallots adds a rich flavor to the whole dish.

#blowfish
The puffer fish was gently grilled over binchotan charcoal.
As the surface dries, the inside becomes more creamy and soft.
The thin sauce made with Suhyangmi risotto and seaweed sauce gives it a Korean-style heartiness, like eating seaweed soup with rice.

#strawberry #chestnut
Seasonal strawberries and chestnuts were pickled in honey, hojicha panna cotta added sweetness, and sheep cheese harmonized the saltiness.

#Michelin 1 star
I visited Goryori Ken after a long time and saw that it was qualified for 1 Michelin star.
I also felt the ever-evolving culinary world of Chef Gun Kim.

PS: I look forward to your great performance in Black and White Chef.

PS2: I really liked the sake Ichie gave me for my wife's birthday. Junmai Daiginjo level made with Yamada Nishiki. Planning to order on my next visit to Ichie

Pour broth with seaweed and wasabi to make ochazuke
All three methods are highly satisfying.

The ratio of rice and eel is just right, so you can eat it without getting tired of it, and the side dishes are also neat. Overall, I have a strong feeling that it is “expensive, but the taste is acceptable.”

reviews.author: Jinwook Kim
reviews.text:
Tsumami comes with crab meat, madai, and aoriika. As Chef Mo said, crab meat prepared by someone else is a delicious ingredient no matter where you go, and personally, I am not a fan of white fish sashimi, but I don't know if my taste buds have changed or if the restaurants I recently visited are good at it, but Sushi Rikyu's madai has a very good flavor and texture. Also, strangely, the sushi restaurants I visited recently did not serve aoriika, which is one of my favorites, but the rich texture and sweetness of the sushi that soothed my disappointment were excellent.

Nigiri begins, and the first piece is shimaaji. You hold it so that you can take a single bite, and the taste is clean and without any unnecessary elements. How can it be so neat? If you think about it, the sharigan is relatively weak, and the amount of shari is a little less (subjective opinion), but if you take just one bite, it mixes perfectly in your mouth, creating a harmony with amylase, shari, and neta, and most of all, you can taste the taste of the raw material because of the appropriate seasoning. I was a bit disappointed with Miss Shari, so I asked her to hold more of her (this is perfect for me). Afterwards, cuttlefish, abalone, and sweet shrimp are served, and they are flawless. Maybe it's because it's so perfect... It's true that if you look at it up to this point, it's hard to find any impact. But, when the tuna comes out, my thoughts change.

As I've always said, I've rarely been satisfied with tuna except for Sushi Koji, but to sum it up, Sushi Rikyu's tuna is crazy. I couldn't eat raw shrimp due to a shellfish allergy, so I skipped it, but I was a little disappointed because they gave me two pieces of akami without asking, but there is a reason. Personally, I don't like the artificial acidity and crunchy texture of akami, but Sushi Rikyu's akami has a moderate acidity and a rich flavor that disappears as soon as you put it in your mouth. Additionally, Otoro is excellent for its unique rich oiliness and cotton candy-like texture. It's been a while since I've had this delicious otoro without any chewy tendons. I don't know if the taste of uni has recently returned, but its unique greenness, sweetness, and coolness are the best, and kohada also has a subtle anchovy scent, which is nice. I think it's my first time eating sardines, but it tastes very good as it has the texture of otoro with the oiliness typical of traditional hikarimono. Lastly, the gyokku is served warm, and it tastes like the most gyokku I've had in a while (other places tasted like bread or pudding), so it's a good way to finish it off.

As the train was running out of time, I was about to quickly finish my meal and get up, but Chef Ryu Ji-sang suggested that I go and have a cup of tea. I felt sorry for refusing, so I watched the tea ceremony, and my mind became calm, and my impatience melted away like snow at the delicious scent and taste of oolong tea. I ask for another drink and stand up. Chef Ryu Ji-sang comes directly to the front of the elevator and greets me until the door closes, but I feel embarrassed inside.

Recently, while visiting a sushi restaurant, out of some sense of obligation (the intention to visit and evaluate all sushi restaurants?), I dared to evaluate the food rather than enjoy it, and the stress that came from that process was considerable, and only today I realize that I was making a mistake again. I invested money and time to enjoy the pleasure of eating, the relaxation gained in the process, and the unique culture of sushi, but unfortunately, I was unable to fully experience it due to various distracting thoughts.

I am truly grateful for today’s visit.

Chef Jeong Ji-young serves all the customers by himself, so it feels a little slow, but you never get bored. It was a lot of fun watching Nigiri.

It was unique that the sushi was placed on black marble, and I think it was a bit difficult to take pictures.

Omakase served well by a chef dressed in proper Japanese attire. It's quite attractive. It wasn't a standardized course every time, so there was a lot of variation and the composition seemed to be very good.

It was nice to be able to taste things that I have never tried before at Tsumami, such as squid, butter-grilled abalone, fried iris, and unagi. Overall, there were many dishes where I thought the sauces and heat control were delicate. Even after so much time has passed, I still remember the crispy skin of unagi.

Tuna accounts for a high proportion of sushi. I was able to eat a variety of tuna, from mid-belly marinated in soy sauce for three days to large belly, negiro, and akami, and I could feel that a lot of attention was paid to the tuna.

In addition, I was able to meet netters that were not easily seen in the middleweight class, such as gasco and crane saury.

In particular, I was able to taste uni, a domestic uni product that is exported to Japan. I was surprised by the refreshing, sweet melting taste that made it difficult to think about what kind of country uni would be exported to Japan. I think it's worth explaining with pride...

The shari is both strong and curly, so it suits my taste very well. This is a great sushi to go with alcohol. It's well worth revisiting next time. I hope to be able to go to a gala dinner someday.

reviews.text:
#Sinsa-dong #Satoshi

“Q: What if I meet a chef who shares the same sushi philosophy as me?”
“A: Becoming a regular”

Chef Gwangwoo Lee opened this restaurant about two years ago based on his experience working as an itamae at the main restaurant of Gangnam's mainstream sushi restaurants such as Sushitatsu and Sushiito. 
He refers to his own sushi style as "self-style," and has earned the nickname "idol of the sushi world" by not missing out on anything from ingredients, techniques, taste, and customer service.

What I felt after experiencing Satoshi
1. Amazing raw material quality
2. Chef’s philosophy of focusing on the taste of raw ingredients
3. Chef’s technique to maximize the taste of raw ingredients
4. Shari walks an exquisite tightrope between hardness and softness.
5. The chef’s hospitality is not awkward even if it’s your first time, but isn’t excessive either.
6. The ultimate in delicacy that captured my heart.

When I write it down like this, it seems like it's the perfect sushi haha.

#material
It is said that 80% of sushi is made up of ingredients and 20% is the technique.
The quality of the raw material determines the taste of sushi, and the more expensive the sushi restaurant, the better the taste. 
The reason why we can say that this place has the highest quality ingredients is that there is no unpleasant smell in the food.
Shiromi is refreshing
Akami is suing
Hikarimono is soggy
Crustaceans are delicious.

Just because it's big doesn't mean it's all delicious, but the bigger the seafood, the more expensive it is and the deeper the taste...
High-quality uni from Sushi Matsumoto, the absolute best sushi restaurant in Korea, and a wholesaler who supplies uni only to this house.
Geumtae used in pot rice has a rich flavor that cannot be produced unless it is larger than 30cm.
Looking at the bread of fried tilefish, it is so thick that discerning sushimeniya can imagine the size of the raw fish.
Ankimo is refreshing, and giant cockle clams, which can be fishy, ​​are refreshing.

There is no compromise on materials.

#technology
The part where my sushi style matches Chef Lee Gwang-woo's style is the technique to maintain the philosophy of taste.
These days, many middle-level sushi restaurants use aburi and charcoal grills. Sushi Koji's Indu Jijim Sababou Zushi is famous, but likes and dislikes are divided.
To be honest, the more expensive the sushi restaurant and the more proud itamae is, the less the use of fire is used.
Although the fire flavor enhances the taste, it also has a bad use in that it kills the subtlety of good ingredients and removes the unpleasant odor of low-fresh ingredients.

Recipes that minimize heat to maximize the taste of ingredients
Appropriate aging method applied to each ingredient
Your own recipe that eliminates the unpleasant smells of ingredients that have bad smells and brings out the taste, etc.
The quality of the ingredients is good, but the technology to bring out the taste of the ingredients is also amazing.

#Shari
I finally realized how much I like the flirty Shari.
The texture of shari has an outstanding texture that I have never felt before.
Each grain of rice is alive, and the elasticity that makes it bounce off your teeth like jelly is truly amazing.
If you're not careful, it can be as hard as uncooked rice, but it creates a bouncy elasticity just at that border.
Moreover, the taste of Shari, which is neither too sour nor too salty, goes well with all netas.
This unprecedented texture of shari is also applied to pot rice, so I received the pot rice of my life as a gift from Chef Lee Gwang-woo.#Hospitality
One of the reasons customers are afraid to go to Sushiya is because they are afraid that the chef will ignore them, such as if it is their first time going, if they are new to sushi, or if they are eating alone....
Or, it could be a vague feeling of anxiety, such as being friendly with regulars but fearing that you will be treated as invisible.
In fact, in order to form a rapport with the chef, the customer must pay close attention to the chef, participate in the conversation, lead the conversation with appropriate sushi knowledge, and even sell alcohol appropriately... There are aspects to all that need to win the chef's favor.
However, Chef Lee Gwang-woo is a person who never gives me this kind of anxiety.
There are four of us in our group and we drink a lot, so even though he may be paying a lot of attention to us, the couple sitting next to us, and even the people eating alone next to them, ask questions and talk to us from time to time, leading the conversation.
Thanks to the chef's hospitality, all seven guests were able to toast together with sake.
It is a place where even first-time visitors can feel at ease.

#manager
The manager is also the best manager ever.
Usually, older women work as managers at sushi restaurants, but Chef Gwang-Woo Lee brought in a top manager who he had been friends with from the beginning and runs the restaurant with him.
It's so delicate, of course, they provide basic friendly service, and they provide service that I've never experienced before. For example, they pay attention to things that get in the way of my chopsticks or hands while eating sushi, and they take care of removing them and rearranging them, showing amazing attention to detail.
The chef in front of the counter serving customers is important, but the ability of the manager behind the counter to support this service also elevates the quality of sushi restaurants, and the manager here is just that.

I don't know if it's the chef's personality, but the composition of omakase is not typical.
It was unique from the first time Judoro was released.
Until now, I've never seen a Sis restaurant that starts with a lineup, but Chef Lee Gwang-woo says he does it just to give you something delicious first haha.
And then he says one more thing...
“Actually, everything is delicious haha.”

- Fishing Yariika (Korean chives) and Tongyeong Haesuuni sauce

#Geumtaepotbap story added.
Life is like golden pot rice.
It doesn't seem like it comes out every time, but fortunately, the customer next to me requested it, so they prepared it.
The fluffy and elastic grains of rice are like shari. The savory taste and the buttery flavor that follows are the highlights of pot rice.
When I asked if they cooked rice with butter, they said that if you cook rice with at least 30-40cm large Geumtae, the fat from Geumtae gives it a savory taste.
The quality of the ingredients is incredible for a small Geumtae.

In conclusion, I fell in love with this house.
I plan to make this place a regular.
It's perfect sushi with nothing missing....
He said he'd give me a king crab leg sashimi next time I go, so I'll have to catch me quickly.

reviews.author: Taiyoon Yoon
reviews.text:
A restaurant with a good overall menu and good value for money.
I made a reservation through Catch Table, and at the time of reservation, I was able to make a reservation in both table and daji format. Formal orders can only be made at a table, so I could make a table reservation the day before, so I made a reservation for 11:30. Luckily, a staff member contacted me a few hours later and said that there was one room available and that I could change it to a room instead of a table, so I was able to dine in the room.
First of all, I was quite satisfied with the overall aspect. When it comes to space, when it comes to space, and when it comes to food, it's food... If you go into detail about the taste, there are definitely some disappointing and lacking parts, but if you think about the price, I could never rate it that much.
For the menu, I ordered set meal B (38,000 won) and was served in the following order: pumpkin porridge, sashimi, sushi, grilled mero, tempura, meal, and dessert.
All meals were satisfactory, but if I were to rank them, it would be mero > sashimi > dessert > sushi = tempura > meal.
Of course, if you had to rank it, that would be the case.
Overall, I was satisfied with everything, but the only disappointing part of the meal was the futomaki. The udon and soba that I ordered were good, but I was disappointed that the ingredients in the futomaki were a bit poor. Other than that, all other menu items were above average.
In particular, looking at the reviews before going, the sashimi sashimi was evaluated well, and it seemed to be good enough to understand why. It seemed like a good compromise between moderate umami and fresh texture. But the best of all was the grilled mero.
It was a grilled mero that had just the right amount of seasoning and had a soft and chewy texture.
I don't have much experience with grilled mero, but I thought it might be difficult to taste a more delicious mero for a while.
The sushi was good, but compared to the previous two menus, it was a bit disappointing. The seasoning of the shari was subtle, and the presence of the neta was not so obvious. The blue-backed fish had a slightly fishy taste. However, I would like to say that this was a very small disappointment and the sushi was good enough.
The tempura was well fried, and the shrimp tempura, which would have been the main dish, was fried quite well. I remember eating it deliciously.
And the dessert was tastier than I expected. It was a blueberry sorbet. Even with the naked eye, I could see ice crystals, so I thought it would be both cool and sour, but when I ate a spoonful, it wasn't like that. The blueberry flavor and savory sweetness spread gently in my mouth, and I could feel the crunching crunch of the ice at the same time. For a moment, I thought that this was something. It was a taste I couldn't imagine.
The more I ate it, the more attractive it tasted, and it suddenly occurred to me that it was possible to create a menu like this at this price thanks to the chef's thought and effort to bring such a difference and twist to even a simple dessert.
This is a house I definitely want to visit again next time.

Cf) First of all, Dachi may have its own charm, but the room was really private and it was nice to be able to eat comfortably. The interior was also neat and tidy, so please note that rooms can be reserved by phone, not through Catch Table.
